We start with the grass, weeds, sunlight, and moisture conditions. Tell us about thin spots or areas that stay wet so we can look beyond color alone.

Visit photos and notes help you follow your lawn’s care. We monitor its response, watch for insect and disease concerns, and explain watering, mowing, or other steps that will support progress.
Care through South Louisiana’s seasons
Lutcher lawns move through spring growth, summer heat, fall transition, and winter weed pressure. We adjust the work to match those conditions, using nutrition when the grass can benefit.
Time feeding to active growth, address early weeds, and use preventive treatments at appropriate seasonal windows.
Adjust nutrition and weed control for heat, moisture, and turf response while monitoring seasonal insect activity.
Shift nutrition as growth slows, manage cool-season weed pressure, and watch for seasonal disease concerns.
Monitor lawn conditions and winter weeds. Dormant warm-season grass does not need the same nitrogen feeding as actively growing summer turf.
This is an overview of seasonal priorities. Actual products, rates, and visit timing depend on turf needs, weather, and label directions.
Know the grass. Match the care.
A sunny Bermuda lawn and shaded centipede grass have different needs. We consider the turf, sunlight, moisture, and maintenance so feeding supports healthy growth without pushing the lawn too hard.
Learn more: LSU AgCenter’s Louisiana Lawn Maintenance guide (PDF) and UF/IFAS centipedegrass guidance .

structured.hero_sub: Your lawn needs care that keeps up with the seasons. Grow Green brings liquid nutrition, targeted weed control, and regular lawn monitoring to Lutcher—with a plan matched to your grass, property, and growing conditions.
structured.local_title: A clear plan for your Lutcher lawn.
structured.local_lead: A sunny Bermuda lawn and shaded centipede grass have different needs. We consider the turf, sunlight, moisture, and maintenance so feeding supports healthy growth without pushing the lawn too hard.

features.title: Understand the lawn
features.body: We start with the grass, weeds, sunlight, and moisture conditions. Tell us about thin spots or areas that stay wet so we can look beyond color alone.

features.title: Apply with purpose
features.body: We feed when your grass can use the nutrients. Weed prevention and targeted treatments work alongside nutrition, with products selected for the turf and conditions.

features.title: See what we did
features.body: Visit photos and notes help you follow your lawn’s care. We monitor its response, watch for insect and disease concerns, and explain watering, mowing, or other steps that will support progress.

real_faqs.q: How often do you treat lawns in Lutcher?
real_faqs.a: Our lawn program includes seasonal planned visits per year, generally about six weeks apart. The applications vary with the season, turf needs, and weather. Your lawn receives an ongoing care program; each visit is not the same fertilizer treatment.

real_faqs.q: How much does the program cost, and how is it billed?
real_faqs.a: Your free estimate is based on the treatable lawn area, property conditions, and selected services. The annual year-round lawn program price is spread across twelve monthly payments. Service is month-to-month with no long-term contract. Monthly billing does not mean a treatment every month.

real_faqs.q: Is weed control included, and what if weeds remain?
real_faqs.a: Yes. Our lawn program combines seasonal weed prevention with targeted control of existing weeds. Established or persistent weeds can require continued management or additional targeted care. If something concerns you between visits, contact our office so we can review it and explain the next step.

real_faqs.q: Which grass types do you treat?
real_faqs.a: We work with centipede, St. Augustine, Bermuda, and zoysia lawns. Grass type, sunlight, moisture, and maintenance guide the nutrition and weed-control choices. If you do not know your turf type, tell us when you request your estimate.

real_faqs.q: Do you serve Gramercy, Paulina, and other nearby communities?
real_faqs.a: Yes. Our service area includes Lutcher, Gramercy, Paulina, Grand Point, Vacherie, North Vacherie, Garyville, and Mount Airy. Send your street address and ZIP code so we can confirm availability for your property and prepare pricing.

real_faqs.q: Do you treat commercial properties in Lutcher?
real_faqs.a: Yes. We serve residential and select commercial properties in Lutcher and the surrounding River Parishes. Mention that the property is commercial in the form notes and include any access or scheduling needs. Our team will confirm the service scope and price.

real_faqs.q: Do I need to be home for treatment?
real_faqs.a: Usually not, as long as we can access the scheduled treatment area. Unlock gates, secure pets, and tell us about access restrictions or sensitive areas. Visit photos and notes document the work, and we provide instructions for caring for the treated lawn.

real_faqs.q: When can children and pets return to the lawn?
real_faqs.a: Keep people and pets away from the treatment area during application. Follow the specific re-entry directions provided for the products used. A single waiting period does not apply to every treatment.

real_faqs.q: Should I water or mow after an application?
real_faqs.a: Follow the instructions provided with that visit. Watering and mowing timing depend on the products applied and the conditions. If you are unsure, contact our office before changing the aftercare plan.

real_faqs.q: How soon will I see results?
real_faqs.a: Response depends on the grass, weeds, weather, and condition of the lawn. Some weeds respond sooner than others, and thin turf needs suitable growing conditions and time to fill in. Mowing, watering, shade, and drainage also affect progress. We explain what to expect and adjust care as we review the lawn.
